input: This passage explains the pump affinity laws, the relations that carry the duty of a centrifugal pump from one speed to another. Their headline consequence is worth stating before the relations themselves: doubling the speed multiplies the shaft power eightfold, and the worked check at the end puts the figure on that claim. The laws compare one pump at two speeds, with the impeller unchanged and the same liquid handled throughout. The flow is proportional to the speed: at twice the speed, the pump delivers twice the flow. The head is proportional to the square of the speed: at twice the speed, the pump develops four times the head. The power is proportional to the cube of the speed: at twice the speed, the shaft takes eight times the power. You use the laws by taking a duty that you know, at a speed that you know, and scaling each quantity by its own power of the speed ratio. Each quantity scales separately, and the common error is to scale the power as if it followed the flow. Worked check: a pump is speeded up until its speed has doubled. The cube of the speed ratio gives the power ratio directly: the shaft power comes out at 8 times its former value, while the flow has only doubled and the head has risen fourfold. A motor that was chosen for the original duty with no margin above it cannot drive the new duty, and that is the decision the check exists to inform.
